sections.hook: What happens when you power rule: $\int x^n dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}+c$? Let's explore indefinite integration (power rule) in IGCSE Add Maths.
sections.core_explanation:
Indefinite Integration (Power Rule)

Power rule: $\int x^n dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}+C$ Integrating polynomials term by term Constant of integration $C$ Integrating $ax^n$ terms Negative and fractional powers Finding $f(x)$ given $f'(x)$
sections.worked_example: Worked example for Indefinite Integration (Power Rule) will demonstrate key concepts step-by-step.
sections.summary: Indefinite Integration (Power Rule) is fundamental for IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 C8.
